selected_problem: Fresh-main reality testing found inferValidationCommands truncated its candidate list to four commands even though runAcceptance already supports up to eight. A repository declaring check, test, lint, typecheck and build could silently omit build; a failing build was therefore able to hide behind four passing earlier scripts and produce a false PASS.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: The committed four-mode router selects DEEP_DEVELOPMENT through the singular evidence-rich central bottleneck gate; no mode rotation was forced.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt is claimed. Selection/routing use committed DWAC source-contract replay over fresh canonical main while the provider remained transiently unavailable.

pre_fix_reproduction.observed: inferValidationCommands returned only the first four commands, runAcceptance executed four passing scripts and returned PASS without running the failing build.

changes: The inference layer now uses the same eight-command upper bound already enforced by runAcceptance instead of silently narrowing evidence to four.
The currently known package plus pyproject heuristics produce at most six commands, so this closes silent truncation for the repository's present inference set while remaining bounded.
A regression proves a failing fifth build command can no longer be omitted behind four passing validation scripts.

validation.tests: 16/16 PASS; 0 skipped on the final POSIX validation run
validation.validation_note: An earlier combined run hit the pre-existing timing-sensitive persistent-PTY cursor test once; an immediate full rerun passed 16/16. The changed acceptance regression was passing in both runs.

truth_boundaries: This aligns current inference with the existing eight-command acceptance bound; it does not claim exhaustive validation discovery for arbitrary monorepos or language/toolchain graphs.
If future inference discovers more than eight commands, an explicit evidence-selection policy will still be required rather than silently claiming exhaustive validation.
The observed persistent-PTY cursor timing flake is outside this acceptance-inference change and remains a separate evidence-quality observation frontier.
This is not an OS-level filesystem/network sandbox; validation workspace confinement remains unresolved.
